name: Gone but Not Forgotten: Dead Media and Lost Gadgets
description: Beta tapes, MiniDiscs, teletext and typewriters: the formats, machines and cures that ruled their day and then vanished.

checkpoints.name: Before the electronic age
checkpoints.note: The slide rule, signal towers, early photographs and one-penny stamps served well for a time. The typewriter, record cylinder and typesetting machine were soon replaced by better methods.

checkpoints.name: The first half of the century
checkpoints.note: Quack medicines such as radium tonics, the iron lung and the whirring spinning-disc television belonged to a world that moved quickly and left some inventions behind.

checkpoints.name: Tapes and format wars
checkpoints.note: Eight-track tapes, Betamax, VHS and LaserDisc fought over the living room, and teletext brought text to television. Format wars left winners, losers and drawers full of tapes.

checkpoints.name: The digital takeover
checkpoints.note: Minitel, MiniDisc and cassette Walkmans, stealth jets and gene-modified tomatoes: some failed and some simply gave way to digital successors.
